brief: JPMorgan's global equity strategy deck stays bullish into year end and argues the case as a chain. Global equities are up 15% year to date in USD total return, EPS revisions have turned outright positive in every region and PMIs are rebounding, so earnings stay a support. Rising bond yields are read as reflecting stronger activity rather than de-anchoring inflation, because wage growth is soft and labour markets are mixed, so central banks deliver less tightening than is priced, so yields do not block equities. A USD that has run as a safe haven and no longer looks cheap then turns lower, which supports international stocks, EM and gold. From that, the note holds equities at 65% versus a 60% benchmark, overweights EM versus DM and the Eurozone within developed markets, keeps the US neutral at 20x forward earnings, and expects Tech/AI not to lead in the second half, so participation broadens into Cyclicals, small caps, Mining, Capital Goods and Semis, ranked over hyperscalers over AI-at-risk plays. December 2026 index targets are MSCI Eurozone 420 and FTSE 100 11,000. Energy stays underweight unless the Iran conflict fully re-escalates.
